newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices end off, short covering dries up.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices end off, short covering dries up.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices ended lower Wednesday reversing earlier gains after short covering in heating oil dried up and crude ran into technical resistance.
"It was as much short covering as it was crude running out of steam at resistance. They all seemed to fall out of bed together," said a New York refined products dealer.
March crude ended off 56 cents a barrel at $21.86 after rising as much as 33 cents to $22.75.
Dealers noted resistance for prompt crude at around $22.80, which was a shelf of spot support established early September before being broken February 7.
March heating oil settled 1.01 cents lower a gallon at 60.85 cents, and March gasoline ended off 1.07 cents a gallon at 62.89 cents.

Prompt heating oil rose as much as 1.74 cents to 63.60 cents Wednesday after weekly oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) Tuesday showed an unexpectedly large decline in distillate stocks.

The API data, which reflects the week ended February 7, said distillate stocks (comprised of heating oil and diesel) fell 4.9 million barrels compared to expectations of a 2.5 million barrel fall, triggering short covering in heat.

The data triggered short covering heating oil while gasoline followed heating oil up. Heating oil and gasoline declined several cents last week on poor refined product demand and a seasonal downturn in oil prices.

"Heating oil had really dropped a lot so you were bound to see a corrective bounce up," said a refined products trader. The trader said heat's earlier gains were also tied to strength in U.S. Gulf cash prices where distillate supplies have tightened.

Unlike heating oil, dealers said fresh long positions were established in gasoline amid the morning rally, but profit-taking set in when heat fell. March gasoline rose as much as 0.94 cent a gallon to 64.90 cents.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
